segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Spain's train crash, missiles over Korea, and a war on edge
bullets: Spain: at least sixty-eight dead after two trains collide
North Korea fires a barrage of missiles
Saudi Arabia, Iran and the Gulf on edge before the U.S. vote

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Thursday, October twenty-ninth.
Tonight we start in Spain, where two high-speed trains collided and the death toll is at least sixty-eight.
Then missiles off North Korea, a Saudi refinery claim nobody has confirmed, and a warning to Gulf allies about Iran. Stay with us.

segments.strap: SPAIN: TWO HIGH-SPEED TRAINS COLLIDE; AT LEAST 68 DEAD
segments.headline: Spain's deadliest train crash in years

graphic.title: Toledo: two trains, 68 dead, search unfinished
bullets: Renfe and Iryo trains collided near Toledo
Regional president: at least 68 dead
Three days of national mourning
Cause not established

lines.text: Two high-speed trains collided Wednesday morning in Toledo province, on the line from Madrid toward Seville. The regional president, Emiliano García-Page, said the death toll had reached sixty-eight by Wednesday afternoon.
He said more victims were likely, because rescuers had not yet reached the bottom of the carriages. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared three days of mourning.

Injury counts do not match. La Nación quotes García-Page at more than one hundred fifty injured, fifteen of them serious. An earlier New York Times update had about eighty injured. Those numbers were not merged.
Renfe says its train left Madrid at eight and hit an Iryo train between Los Yébenes and Urda. Why is the open question, and the accounts disagree.
One official says a control system called L.Z.B. failed around eight-thirty after a communication fault in three network computers, leaving sixty-three kilometers without that safety layer.

A source close to the investigation told Reuters the Iryo had been stopped on an order from the track operator because of a signalling failure, and was then hit. Other officials point to an error at central command.
No agency has called it a cyber attack, and no court has found anything. Those are four accounts, not a finding.
The New York Times and La Nación both report another fatal collision on this line within the past year. That is the papers' background.

segments.strap: NORTH KOREA FIRES ABOUT A DOZEN SHORT-RANGE MISSILES
segments.headline: Missiles from Wonsan

graphic.title: Short-range barrage, about 250 km
bullets: Fired from the Wonsan area around 12:30 p.m. Thursday
Counts: about 10 (Reuters), about a dozen (Yonhap)
Japan: did not appear to land in its zone
17th ballistic launch this year

lines.text: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff say North Korea fired short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area at about twelve-thirty Thursday afternoon, toward the East Sea. They flew about two hundred fifty kilometers.
The count depends on who is counting. Reuters says around ten. Yonhap says about a dozen. The Korea Herald says more than ten.
Japan's Defense Ministry says the missiles did not appear to land inside Japan's exclusive economic zone.

Seoul called an emergency security meeting and called the launch a serious violation of United Nations resolutions. A military official told Yonhap he believes the KN-twenty-five was involved. That identification is his alone.
On the Korea Herald's count, it is the year's seventeenth ballistic launch and the first in seventeen days.
South Korea's stock market jumped more than six percent Wednesday. More on that in a moment.

segments.strap: HOUTHIS CLAIM RAS TANURA HIT; SAUDIS HAVE NOT CONFIRMED
segments.headline: Saudi Arabia: claims, intercepts and oil

graphic.title: Ras Tanura: claim, no confirmation
bullets: Houthis claim a direct refinery strike; Saudis have not confirmed
Saudis: two missiles at Riyadh intercepted
Houthi-run media: 14 killed at Al-Hazm market
Brent settled at $115.32

lines.text: The Houthis claim they hit the Ras Tanura refinery in Saudi Arabia. Saudi authorities have not confirmed a direct hit. A fire near the site was reported and contained, and damage and loading effects are unclear.

Saudi officials say two missiles aimed at Riyadh were intercepted, and falling debris damaged a building, a construction site and a vehicle. The Houthi claim of hitting the Defense Ministry is not verified.

Now the other side. Houthi-run media say Saudi airstrikes hit a public market and a fuel station in Al-Hazm, in Yemen's Al-Jawf province. They say at least fourteen people were killed, women and children among them.
Other Houthi-aligned outlets give thirteen dead and sixteen hurt, or fourteen dead and fifteen hurt. Xinhua says it could not verify any of it. Saudi Arabia had no immediate comment.

Oil is pricing the fear either way. Reuters says Brent settled up one percent at one hundred fifteen dollars and thirty-two cents a barrel. U.S. crude rose three percent to one hundred two dollars and seventy-eight cents.

segments.strap: U.S. WARNS GULF ALLIES OF POSSIBLE IRAN STRIKES AFTER NOV. 3 VOTE
segments.headline: The warning to Gulf allies

graphic.title: Strikes after the election? The warning, the cost, the firing
bullets: AP: allies told to prepare for possible strikes after Nov. 3
Pentagon war-cost estimate: $47.1 billion
Hegseth fires Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, a top Joint Staff planner
Advocacy group: 53 laden Iranian tankers

lines.text: The Associated Press reports that U.S. officials warned Gulf allies to prepare for possible strikes on Iran after the November third election. The timing of any military readiness remains unclear. Those are officials, speaking to AP.
AP also reports the Pentagon's war-cost estimate to Congress has reached forty-seven point one billion dollars.

Also from AP: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, who directed strategy, plans and policy for the Joint Staff. No reason was given and no replacement was named. He is the second general removed from that post under Hegseth.
The same reporting places the firing while President Trump weighs renewed strikes.

The shipping picture is a claim from an advocacy group, United Against Nuclear Iran. It says at least fifty-three oil-laden Iranian tankers are still near Iran, while twenty empty Iran-flagged tankers sit off Sri Lanka. That is not a customs or port-authority count.
Tehran has not spoken in today's reporting that we have. We will say so when it does.

segments.strap: OLESHKY PAUSE HOLDS 30 HOURS; RUSSIA SAYS 613 DRONES AIMED AT MOSCOW
segments.headline: Ukraine: a local pause, a big night

graphic.title: Oleshky quiet; Moscow drone wave claimed
bullets: Both ombudsmen: no incidents in 30 hours
Demining under way; aid not reported delivered
Moscow mayor: most of 613 drones downed
Kharkiv struck overnight, school damaged

lines.text: In Oleshky, the local ceasefire is holding so far. Ukraine's ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, said thirty hours passed without a single incident. Russia's ombudsman, Yana Lantratova, said the same. Kherson's regional administration reported no incoming strikes in the preceding day.

This is a pause in one city, not a general ceasefire. Demining of routes is under way. Food and medicine have not been reported delivered, and an evacuation is still a plan for Friday. The pause is stated to end late on November first.

Then the night. Moscow's mayor, Sergei Sobyanin, says Russia downed most of six hundred thirteen drones heading toward the capital. Al Jazeera, citing TASS, says two hundred thirty-one were destroyed on approach to the city.
An earlier Kyiv Independent count was fifty-seven intercepted, with flight limits at three Moscow airports. Those numbers were not merged. No independent damage count is available.
In Kharkiv, Mayor Ihor Terekhov says Russia struck the city and damaged an educational institution. No toll was given.
Oleshky is quiet. Moscow and Kharkiv were not.

segments.strap: ISRAEL: NO BLOC HAS 61 SEATS WITH 85.6% COUNTED
segments.headline: Israel's count is still open

graphic.title: 85.6% counted: 53 / 48 / 19
bullets: Netanyahu's bloc 53; Eisenkot's bloc 48; Arab parties 19
Likud leads parties with 26 seats
About 600,000 absentee ballots outstanding
Final results due Thursday, maybe Friday

sources.name: JTA, relaying the Central Elections Committee

lines.text: Israel's election count is still open. With eighty-five point six percent counted, the Central Elections Committee puts Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc at fifty-three seats, Gadi Eisenkot's bloc at forty-eight, and the Arab parties at nineteen.
Likud leads all parties with twenty-six seats. A party called Yashar has twenty-one. Every bloc is short of sixty-one, the number needed for a majority.
About six hundred thousand absentee ballots are still outstanding. Final results are expected Thursday evening, though the double-envelope counting could run into Friday.
A preliminary seat count is not a government. Nobody has been certified, and no coalition exists yet.

segments.strap: FLÁVIO BOLSONARO IN MIAMI, CALLS HIMSELF 'RIGHTFUL LEADER'
segments.headline: Brazil: the loser in Miami

graphic.title: Bolsonaro in Miami; markets slide again
bullets: Lands at Opa-locka, 9:20 a.m. Wednesday
Calls himself rightful leader; accuses court and Lula of an electoral coup
Lula won 51.79% to 48.21%
Ibovespa −2.68% at 171,006

lines.text: Flávio Bolsonaro is in the United States. El País reports his plane landed at Opa-locka airport north of Miami at nine-twenty Wednesday morning, after a route through Argentina.

Reuters says he declared himself Brazil's rightful leader and accused the Supreme Court and President Lula of an electoral coup. He first posted a letter calling himself the elected president, deleted it, and posted a softer version. Brazil's electoral court counted Lula at fifty-one point seven nine percent.

The travel is contested. O Globo and CNN Brasil say a U.S. record shows entry on a diplomatic passport Brazil had already cancelled. Brazil's Federal Police say they have no record of him leaving the country. No arrest warrant has been reported.

Markets are not calm. Brazil's main stock index fell two point six eight percent to one hundred seventy-one thousand and six, the third session since the runoff. Banks led it down. The dollar sat near five dollars thirty-four reais.

segments.strap: DOJ ACTIONS BEFORE MIDTERMS; JUDGE DENIES CALIFORNIA BALLOT REQUEST
segments.headline: Midterms, one week out

graphic.title: Week before the vote: DOJ, courts, rallies
bullets: AP: DOJ moves include a search of Rep. Omar's home
Judge denies DOJ bid to halt California ballot processing
Trump in Ohio, Obama in Georgia
Voters cite record fuel prices

lines.text: The midterms are next Tuesday, and the Justice Department is in the story. The Associated Press lists October actions including a search of Representative Ilhan Omar's home, charges against two former F.B.I. officials, a renewed attempt to prosecute James Comey, and an unsuccessful attempt to indict Cassidy Hutchinson.
Critics challenge the timing. The Justice Department says it is following the facts and the law.

In court, U.S. District Judge David Carter denied the department's request to stop California from processing ballots for up to twenty thousand people it alleges are likely noncitizens. The department says it will appeal.
In Boston, a federal judge granted a ten-day stay blocking a new refugee rule that cut the response time to a termination notice from thirty days to ten, Axios reports.
On the trail, Trump campaigned in Chillicothe, Ohio, while Barack Obama rallied with Georgia Democrats outside Atlanta. AP says voters are confronting record fuel prices and rising costs.
Prices are the thread tonight.

segments.strap: FED HOLDS 3.75–4.00% ON 10–2 VOTE; CANADA RAISES RATES
segments.headline: Two central banks, two answers

graphic.title: Fed holds; Bank of Canada hikes
bullets: Fed: hold, two dissenters wanted a hike
Bank of Canada: +0.25 point to 2.5%, first rise since 2023
Bank of Japan meets today

lines.text: The Federal Reserve held its target at three and three-quarters to four percent. The vote was ten to two. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack wanted a quarter-point increase. The statement said inflation remained elevated.

Our blind-spot check found the other decision. The Bank of Canada raised its overnight rate a quarter point to two and a half percent, its first increase since July twenty twenty-three. Governor Tiff Macklem said the inflation outlook has worsened, with the Middle East war pushing oil higher for longer.

On Wall Street, the S&P five hundred rose point three percent to seven thousand seven hundred forty-four. The Dow rose to fifty-two thousand four hundred seventy-five, the Nasdaq to twenty-six thousand five hundred fifty. Per AP, the two-year Treasury yield rose after the Fed, then reversed.
Bitcoin is near eighty thousand dollars. Coinbase's price this morning was seventy-nine thousand eight hundred sixty, and that is one exchange's print.
The Bank of Japan starts its meeting today, and its decision lands tomorrow.

segments.strap: UK BUDGET: BANK SURCHARGE TO 6%, £100 ENERGY PAYMENT
segments.headline: Britain's first Healey Budget

graphic.title: Healey Budget: banks pay more, bills fall
bullets: Banks' surcharge 3% → 6% for 15 months from January
£100 energy payment, 20 million households
Electricity VAT cut to July; gas standing charges removed

lines.text: In London, Chancellor John Healey delivered his first Budget. The BBC notes it is the first under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
He said headroom against the government's fiscal rule is fifteen billion pounds in twenty twenty-nine to thirty, rising to twenty-two billion the year after.
To pay for energy help, banks face an extra three percent on their surcharge, taking it to six percent, from January for fifteen months.

For households: a hundred-pound energy payment for twenty million homes in council tax bands A to D. The electricity V.A.T. cut runs to July, which Healey says takes fifty pounds off the price cap. Gas standing charges come off bills. Fuel duty stays frozen until July.
On housing, an extra one billion pounds for social homes, and government-backed loans for first-time buyers.
Markets shrugged. The FTSE one hundred closed at ten thousand six hundred ninety-four, up a hair. Banks rose because the surcharge was six percent, not the eight that was feared. Housebuilders fell.

segments.strap: SOUTH KOREA'S KOSPI JUMPS 6.6% ON CHIP RALLY
segments.headline: Asia: chips, an IPO and a plenum

graphic.title: KOSPI +6.63%; Jio lists 27% above issue
bullets: KOSPI +6.63% to 6,012; buy-side sidecar triggered
SK hynix +10.89%, Samsung +9.01%
Jio Platforms closes first day 26.81% above issue
China's plenum scheduled to end today

lines.text: Asia had a big Wednesday, mostly in chips. South Korea's KOSPI jumped six point six three percent to six thousand twelve. SK hynix rose nearly eleven percent and Samsung nine percent. A five-minute buying halt, called a sidecar, triggered in the morning.

SK hynix posted preliminary third-quarter operating profit of eighty-three trillion won, announced about one hundred trillion won of shareholder returns for the year, and said its next-generation H.B.M.4 memory should outsell the older version this quarter.
In Japan, Advantest raised its full-year profit guidance, citing demand for A.I. chip testing.
In India, Jio Platforms closed its first session at fourteen hundred nineteen rupees, twenty-six point eight one percent above its issue price. The main Sensex index slipped half a percent.
In Hong Kong, DSBJ opened below its offer price and closed less than one percent below it.
China's party plenum is scheduled to end today. No final communiqué had appeared at the cutoff.

segments.strap: ALPHABET CLOUD REVENUE DOUBLES; MICROSOFT AZURE UP 48%
segments.headline: Big Tech reports

graphic.title: Alphabet and Microsoft report
bullets: Alphabet Q3 revenue $127.6B (+25%); Cloud $30.7B (+103%)
Gemini app hits one billion users
Microsoft revenue $92.3B (+19%); Azure +48%
Alphabet shares fell after hours; Microsoft rose ~3%

lines.text: Two giants reported. Alphabet's third-quarter revenue was one hundred twenty-seven point six billion dollars, up twenty-five percent. Google Cloud revenue was thirty point seven billion, up one hundred three percent. The Gemini app reached one billion users.
Alphabet says its model A.P.I.s process nearly thirty-two billion tokens a minute. Per AP, its shares fell after hours because results came in below Wall Street expectations.

Microsoft reported ninety-two point three billion dollars in revenue, up nineteen percent. Azure grew forty-eight percent, and contracted future cloud revenue reached six hundred seventy-seven billion dollars. AP says its shares gained nearly three percent.

From The Verge, all claims by the companies or executives: Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon with a leap in cybersecurity. Instagram's Adam Mosseri says negativity about A.I. is going to get worse. Anduril says its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch.
The tokens-per-minute figure is the number to watch.

segments.strap: NAIROBI: 16 STILL MISSING IN EASTLEIGH COLLAPSE
segments.headline: Eastleigh, day six

graphic.title: 16 missing; two people detected, not reached
bullets: Missing count fell from 20 to 16 after verification
Phone data places nine at the site
Rescuers say 80% of debris cleared
Detectives question developer and officials

lines.text: In Nairobi's Eastleigh district, sixteen people are still missing six days after a building collapsed. Citing the regional commissioner, Nation reports the number fell from twenty to sixteen after verification, and phone signals suggest nine were inside.
Rescuers say about eighty percent of the debris is cleared. They have not reached two people whose signs of life were detected more than a day earlier. A detection is not a rescue.

Detectives have questioned one developer and county, building-inspectorate and construction-authority officials. No death toll is confirmed, and storey counts of the building range from thirteen to eighteen across reports.

segments.strap: CDC WIDENS EBOLA AIR-TRAVEL ORDER; AFRICA CDC MEETS MINISTERS
segments.headline: Ebola: new travel rule, three case counts

graphic.title: U.S. travel attestation widens Nov. 3
bullets: CDC: all people on U.S.-bound flights attest no DRC stay
Effective 11:59 p.m. EST Nov. 3
Africa CDC convenes health ministers
Kenya: nine confirmed, two dead

lines.text: The C.D.C. amended its Ebola order. It now covers all people on U.S.-bound international aircraft, including crew. From eleven-fifty-nine p.m. Eastern on November third, they must attest they have not been in the Democratic Republic of Congo in the past twenty-one days.
Africa C.D.C. convened an urgent virtual meeting of African health ministers Wednesday. Its chief, Jean Kaseya, said around five thousand people have died across four countries.

The case counts do not agree. Tuesday's wires said ten thousand sixty confirmed cases and four thousand eight hundred eighty-seven deaths. One tracker reads a later bulletin at ten thousand one hundred ninety-three and four thousand nine hundred sixty. Kaseya's number is a third. They are three figures, not one.
Kenya reports nine confirmed cases and two deaths, with no new case in Wednesday's reporting.

segments.strap: U.S. SANCTIONS RWANDA'S DEFENCE MINISTRY OVER M23 SUPPORT
segments.headline: Africa: sanctions, a strike and a gas find

graphic.title: Rwanda sanctioned; Darfur strike claimed
bullets: OFAC sanctions Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama
Treasury: thousands of Rwandan troops in the Kivus
Darfur: five reported killed near El Geneina
Tanzania: first big gas find in a decade

lines.text: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned Rwanda's Ministry of Defence and a credit society called Zigama. Secretary Scott Bessent said Rwanda must stop supporting the M23 rebels and withdraw its troops from eastern Congo. Treasury says thousands of Rwandan troops are operating in North and South Kivu. Kigali's reply was not available.

In Sudan's West Darfur, Radio Tamazuj reports five people killed in an airstrike near El Geneina airport. An official of the R.S.F.-aligned local government blames a Sudanese Army drone on October twenty-sixth. The army has not responded. That is one side's account.
In Egypt, a court fined Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah three million pounds and ordered the independent news site closed. She was released after paying and says she will appeal.
One good-news item: Tanzania announced an estimated two hundred twenty-three billion cubic feet of gas at a well in Mnazi Bay, its first major discovery in a decade.

segments.strap: UN VOTE AGAINST U.S. CUBA EMBARGO PASSES 130–17
segments.headline: Cuba: the annual UN vote

graphic.title: 130 in favor, 17 against, 25 abstain
bullets: Last year's tally: 165–7–12
Germany and Italy abstained
U.S.: 'There is no blockade'
Cuba in a severe energy crisis

lines.text: The U.N. General Assembly again voted to condemn the U.S. embargo on Cuba: one hundred thirty in favor, seventeen against, twenty-five abstaining. Last year it was one sixty-five to seven, with twelve abstentions.
Germany and Italy abstained. Al Jazeera notes both had voted in favor before.
The U.S. ambassador, Mike Waltz, said major economies had shifted. He told the Assembly, quote, there is no blockade, and blamed Cuba's troubles on its own government.

Cuba's foreign minister, Bruno Rodríguez, said the United States was isolated again while trying to strangle the Cuban people. U.N. News describes the island as in a severe energy crisis, which it ties to a U.S. fuel embargo.
The vote is symbolic. It does not repeal the embargo.

segments.strap: KING TIDES FLOOD COASTS; CYCLONE ARNAB KILLS 3 IN INDIA
segments.headline: Floods, a cyclone and a fading storm

graphic.title: King tides, Arnab, Vance
bullets: King tides flood California, Florida, Carolinas
NWS: 1–2 ft inundation on Outer Banks; NC-12 closed at Rodanthe
Arnab: 3 dead, 31 houses, 57,000 in relief camps
Vance now a depression, no watches

lines.text: King tides flooded streets, homes and businesses along coastal California, Florida and the Carolinas, AP reports. A section of Pacific Coast Highway in Orange County was shut. The National Weather Service cites one to two feet of water in low-lying parts of North Carolina's Outer Banks, and N.C.-twelve is closed near Rodanthe.

In India, Cyclone Arnab weakened to a severe cyclonic storm after crossing near Yanam. The disaster force's preliminary report is three deaths in Andhra Pradesh, thirty-one houses damaged, and about fifty-seven thousand people in relief camps.
Off Mexico, Vance is a tropical depression with thirty-five mile an hour winds, expected to go post-tropical within a day. No coastal watches or warnings are posted.

In the western Pacific, Typhoon In-fa is on the Japan Meteorological Agency's active list. A tracking site shows winds near two hundred fifteen kilometers an hour. That is the tracker's display, not the agency's own figure.

segments.strap: GMO OFFERS $1M BOUNTY OVER CLOUD BREACH; HACKER CLAIMED AT DHS
segments.headline: Cyber: a bounty and a leak

graphic.title: GMO bounty; DHS records claim
bullets: GMO: 113 tips in six hours
Up to 26,739 servers potentially affected
No malware confirmed on devices analyzed so far
The Verge: hacker took 40,000+ DHS records

lines.text: Japan's GMO Internet Group has opened a bounty of up to one million dollars for information leading to the arrest of whoever attacked its Onamae Desktop Cloud service. It says twenty-six thousand seven hundred thirty-nine servers were potentially affected, and that does not mean all were breached.
In six hours the bounty site received one hundred thirteen tips. GMO says analysis of customer devices has not confirmed malware or ransomware, and its investigation continues.

In the U.S., The Verge reports that a hacker stole more than forty thousand employee records from the Department of Homeland Security. That is the outlet's report, and the government's account was not in our sources.

segments.strap: BREWERS WIN FIRST WORLD SERIES, BEAT RAYS 4–1 IN GAME 5
segments.headline: Milwaukee wins it all

graphic.title: Brewers win the World Series
bullets: Game 5: Milwaukee 4, Tampa Bay 1
First championship in club history
Misiorowski: 5⅔ scoreless innings
SoftBank sweeps Japan Series

lines.text: Milwaukee won its first World Series. The Brewers beat Tampa Bay four to one in Game Five. Jacob Misiorowski threw five and two-thirds scoreless innings.
In Japan, SoftBank beat DeNA four to two to sweep the Japan Series. It is the Hawks' thirteenth title and their second straight.

In England's League Cup, Liverpool and Chelsea drew one-one, Manchester City and Brighton two-two, Bournemouth beat Aston Villa three-nil, and Sunderland beat Brentford three-two. In Serie A, Bologna won four-two at Milan and Inter won two-nil at Venezia.
In the N.F.L., the Patriots visit Miami in Week Eight. New England lists A.J. Brown among players limited. Miami lists two players with concussion-related status as not participating.
In Korea, Samsung visits KIA tonight for Game Three of the playoff series, tied after Samsung's Game Two win.

segments.strap: ALSO TODAY: AUSTRALIA CASINO FINE, FRANCE PROTESTS, TRUCKING AND MORE
segments.headline: Also today

graphic.title: The quick hits
bullets: Star Entertainment fined A$260 million
French students plan marches Oct. 31 and Nov. 5
Australia's inflation 4.3%
UPS plans 5.9% average rate rise Dec. 21

lines.text: Quick hits. A federal court in Australia ordered Star Entertainment to pay two hundred sixty million Australian dollars for money-laundering breaches. The regulator had sought four hundred million.
Australia's inflation rate rose to four point three percent in September, from four.
In France, student leaders vow marches on October thirty-first and November fifth, after a government education offer, according to the Deseret News.
Stellantis shares jumped fifteen percent after a four-hundred-fifty-three-million-euro loss that analysts called in line.
Petrobras reports record exports and third-quarter output up nearly twelve percent.
UPS plans an average five point nine percent rate increase from December twenty-first, while truckload capacity stays tight.
NASA logged a gamma-ray burst, detected October twenty-fourth, seen by several space telescopes.
In entertainment, Clayface led the weekend box office, and Jailer 2 has passed seven hundred fifty crore rupees worldwide.
And Apple is charging fourteen thousand five hundred forty-nine dollars for a fully specced touchscreen MacBook Pro, per The Verge.
